purpose: Hand-authored input to tools/build_challenge_families.py (GOAL-WORKBENCH-16 slice 2). It names which repository evidence supports each proposed exam setting and how a client's words are matched to a launch-portfolio family. Every quote must appear verbatim in its source file; the generator refuses one that does not. Nothing here is a scientific value: settings are relayed from the exam-design campaign's own recommendations, and their status stays the readiness record's.
matching_rule: A family is suggested when the client's own words, component names or input and output names contain one of its keywords, or its physical processes overlap the client's. Suggestions are ranked by the number of distinct keywords matched, then by physics overlap. A suggestion is a starting point for Carbon review, not an assessment of fit.

battery-exam-design-campaign-1.title: Exam-design campaign 1 (battery), 2026-09-24
battery-exam-design-campaign-1.summary: A bounded development campaign that solved 2,604 battery references without a failure, tested the gates against authored faults, replayed the exam loop over nine batch and rotation settings, and verified a frozen comparison rule on 200 private cases. It is public/synthetic DEVELOPMENT research: nothing in it is scientifically, security or production qualified.

settings.label: Public training set
settings.why: Model error was still falling at 400 cases: the competent recipe improved about a third from 200 to 400, and 400 references cost about USD 0.58 to solve.
settings.section: 2. How much public training data is a useful starting point?

settings.label: Screening batch size
settings.value: 100 parent cases per batch, 3 batches active (a 300-case pool)
settings.why: Batch 100 ranked models most like the fresh finalist cases (Kendall tau 0.93), and a 300-case pool separated two equal-quality models beyond the margin only 3.5 % of the time, against 9.6 % for a 150-case pool.
settings.section: 4. Screening versus fresh finalist outcomes; 5. Reconstruction variability
table_columns: Kendall tau with fresh finalist ranking
supporting_columns: Equal-quality models separated beyond the margin

settings.label: Rotation
settings.value: Retire the oldest batch after 3 admitted submissions
settings.why: A scripted attacker that learns only from the aggregate score gained 0.3 % at batch 100 and rotation after 3, far below the 5.7 % margin. Rotation is set conservatively because adaptive agents were not measured.
quotes: **Recommendation: batch 100, rotate after 3.** Rotation is set conservatively for

settings.label: Equivalence margin
settings.why: Reseeding the same recipe moved its score by up to 2.8 % (standard deviation), so a smaller margin would promote noise. The price: an improvement near the margin was found about half the time.
quotes: **The equivalence margin** is 2 × the largest seed SD, which is **5.7 %**.

settings.label: What can be promoted
settings.value: Only a fresh-case IMPROVEMENT; a regression in the important region blocks promotion
settings.why: Screening alone was fooled by every memorizing candidate, but the fresh finalist comparison promoted none of them, promoted the real improvement every time, and made no false promotion.
quotes: | Pool-leak memorization (truth: equivalent) | nominated 27 / 27 (screening is fooled); **promoted 0 / 27**; the fresh final comparison catches it |
| Regional regression `mlp_localized` (overall +4.4 %, important region worse) | never nominated |

settings.label: Physical gates
settings.value: Initial voltage, voltage ceiling and floor, initial temperature, capacity bound, paired repeat, finite output
settings.why: Each authored fault was rejected by its own gate on all 600 screening cases, while correct predictions of plating and hot operating conditions were never failed.
settings.section: 3. Gates: behaviour, failures and coverage gaps
quotes: | +20 mV on the 4.2 V hold | `voltage_ceiling` | 600 / 600 fail |

settings.label: Compute cost per submission
settings.value: About USD 0.001 to screen one submission; about USD 0.29 per finalist comparison
settings.why: Measured on one A40 pod. Screening is cheap; the fresh references for a finalist comparison dominate.
quotes: | **Screening one submission** (batch 100, pool 300) | one GPU reconstruction + inference + scoring | **≈ USD 0.001** (USD 0.011 on the CPU backend) |
| **Batch build** | 100 references | **USD 0.14**, amortized over 3 submissions = USD 0.047 |
| **Finalist comparison** | 2 reconstructions + 200 fresh references + inference | **≈ USD 0.29**, dominated by the fresh references |
